Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http Ilwmv. dilg.gov.ph DILG Legal opinion No. 19 S. 2016 ASEC JOSEFINA CASTILLA-GO Concurrent OIC, DILG-Region IV-A 3/F Andenson Building I, Brgy. Parian 27 APR 2016 Calamba City, Laguna DIR. DARRELL 1. DIZON Provincial Director, DILG-Rizal 3rd Floor, Rizal Capitol Compound Building Antipolo City, Rizal Gentleman and Lady: This has reference to the following: I. Letter dated 21 January 2016 of PD Darrell I . Dizon posing this query: "Will the Mayor, upon the expiration/lifting of the preventive suspension and upon his REASSUMPTION receive the full salary or compensation including emoluments during the April I -June 29, 2015 suspension pendentelite?" 2. Memorandum dated 19 October 2015 of DILG-Region IV-A Director Renato L. Brion requesting the Central Office's guidance on whether the salaries, benefits and privileges of the suspended mayor will be due to the acting municipal mayor. As culled from the documents forwarded to the Central Office, hereunder are the relevant factual antecedents On 25 March 2015, the Resolution dated II February 2015 of the Sandiganbayan (4th Division) in Criminal Case No. SB-08-CRM-0375 entitled "People of the Philippines vs. Leandro V. Masikip and Tomas N. Aguirre" (Mayor and Vice-Mayor, respectively, of Pililla, Rizal) was implemented. Thus, Mayor Masikip was preventively suspended for a period of ninety (90) days;

In view thereof, Vice-Mayor Richard Sia', assumed as Acting Mayor pursuant to Section 462 of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991; Thereafter, Acting Mayor Sia wrote DILG-region IV-A requesting clarification on whether upon his assumption as Acting Mayor, he is entitled to the salaries, benefits and privileges of suspended Mayor Masikip; DILG-Region IV-A Director Renato L. Brion sent a Memorandum dated 19 October 2015 to the Central Office requesting guidance on whether the salaries, benefits and privileges of the suspended mayor will be due to the acting municipal mayor. In his aforesaid Memorandum, RD Brion represented that DILG-CAR issued Opinion No. 03, series of 1999 affirming that the Acting Mayor is entitled to compensation, remuneration and other emoluments attached by law to the office. Pertinent portion of the aforesaid DILG-CAR opinion is quoted hereunder, thus: "Upon the automatic assumption of Hon. Agcongay to the Office of the Mayor, she is mandated to exercise the powers of the Office and perform the duties and functions attached thereto. Corollary thereto, she is automatically entitled to the benefits and all other emoluments attached to the Office. It would be an outright derogation of public policy and the fundamental precepts of fair play if we would construe the quoted provision to impose only the obligations and functions of the Office to the vice mayor without granting also the privileges and benefits of the said Office. A basic rule in statutory construction states that laws shall be interpreted in such a way that public policy and justice shall be upheld. This elementary precept is very much applicable in the case at bar, considering that Hon. Agcongay has been performing the duties and function of the Mayor for more than a year. ' 1 Duly elected Vice-Mayor for the term 2013-2016. 2 Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, Or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave Of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days.

RD Brion further represented that DILG-CAR Opinion No. 03, series of 1999 was based on a notion on Section 46 of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 and Section 1913 of COA Circular No. 91-368, GAAM, Volume 1. However, DILG-region I V -A (CALABARZON) has an adverse view on the matter. They are of the position that entitlement of salaries, compensation, remuneration and emoluments do apply to elective local officials who assumed the next higher position by virtue of Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991 on temporary vacancy in the office of the local chief executive, based on the following: a. b. c. The assumption to the Office of the Mayor in an acting capacity by virtue of Section 46, in relation to Section 445 (4), of the Local Government Code of 1991 is already defined as part and parcel of the powers, duties and compensation of the vice-mayor. The idea is that, the person is not acting a function that is beyond to what he was elected because to assume as the acting vice-mayor is a duty that has been established by law and being compensated accordingly, regardless the temporary vacancy shall occur. Section 191 of COA Circular No. 91-368, GAAM, Volume I, will not apply because the assumption in the temporary vacancy do not require appointment but automatic operation of law. The assumed position, mayor, on the other hand, is not an appointive position but an elective position. Mayor Masikip was preventively suspended for alleged violation of Republic Act No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. Section 13 of the aforesaid law provides: Section 13. Suspension and loss of benefits.—Any incumbent public officer against whom any criminal prosecution under a valid information under this At or under Title Seven Book [I of the Revised Penal Code or for any offense in volving fraud upon government or public funds or property whether as a simple or as complex offense and in whatever stage of execution and mode of participation, is pending in court shall be suspended from office. Should he be convicted by final judgment, he shall lose 3 Sec. 191. Basic Requirements—The basic requirements for payment of salaries and wages are: E. F. G. H. Existence of legally created position with fixed compensation or emolument attached to the position; Issuance of a valid appointment; Rendition Of service being paid; ad Payment to the right person.

all retirement or gratuity benefits under any law, but if he is acquitted, he shall be entitled to reinstatement and to the salaries and benefits which he failed to receive during suspension, unless in the meantime administrative proceedings have been filed against him. In sum, the objective of herein requests of RD Brion and PD Dizon is for the Central Office to reconcile or, if not, resolve the conflicting positions between DILG-Region I V -A and DILG-CAR. May it be respectfully informed that in a letter dated IO November 2015 to Hon. Protacio C. Pena of the Municipality of Goa, Camarines Sur, the Central Office addressed a similar issue, that is, whether the Acting Mayor is entitled to the salary and other benefits ofa duly elected mayor considering the Tact that he has been performing the duties and functions of the position Tora period ofalmostsix (6) months. The Central Office answered the aforesaid issue in this wise: "xxx we reiterate DILG Opinion No. 18 s. 2001 dated 26 March 2001 wherein a 'vice mayor cannot validly claim the salary pertaining to the office of' the mayor because the exercise of the powers and performance of the duties and Tunctions of the mayor is merely brought about by the temporary absence of the latter (Sec. 46 [a], Local Government Code). It is just an additional function or duty of the vice mayor and as such, he is not entitled to any further remuneration (Sec. 445 [a], Local Government Code). " Thus, following the aforecited opinion, an Acting Mayor is not entitled to the salary ofa duly elected mayor. " (Emphasis Supplied) The aforesaid letter to Hon. Pefia is the latest position of the Central Office on the matter. A copy of said letter is hereto attached for your ready reference. In this regard, all previous opinions and/or positions issued relative to the same subject matter which are inconsistent herewith are hereby modified and/or revoked accordingly. As to the additional query posed by PD Dizon in his letter dated 21 January 2016, the same was already addressed by DILG-Region IV-A in its Memorandum dated 19 October 2015. Mayor Masikip was preventively suspended for alleged violation of Republic Act No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. Upon expiration/lifting of his preventive suspension and/or re-assumption to office, he cannot claim his full salary or compensation during the time that he was suspended from office. Such non-receipt of full salary or compensation being a necessary consequence of suspension.

However, if accused Masikip is thereafter acquitted, Section 13 of RA 3019 provides that he shall be entitled to reinstatement and to the salaries and benefits which he failed to receive during suspension, unless in the meantime administrative proceedings have been filed against him. Thank you. V ruly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary Is/17 - OUSLG 20 '(PO 4-22-01942 Copy furnished: RD MARLO IRINGAN Regional Director, DILG-CAR Barangay Center, Baguio City
